reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: The principal calculations and graph descriptions are correct. Series 1 gives s=(0.50 m/s)t and v=0.50 m/s. Series 2 gives a=0.40 m/s², v=(0.40 m/s²)t and s=(0.20 m/s²)t²; successive displacements are 0.05, 0.15, 0.25, 0.35 and 0.45 m. At 2.0 s, average velocity is 0.80/2.0=0.40 m/s, half the instantaneous 0.80 m/s. Predictions are 5.0 m and 0.50 m/s for the car, and 1.8 m and 1.2 m/s for the cart. The cart remains on its 2.0 m track; the model reaches its end at approximately 3.162 s. With the stipulated g=10 m/s², fall distances at 0.20/0.40/0.60 s are 0.20/0.80/1.80 m and velocities are 2.0/4.0/6.0 m/s. The last value describes arrival immediately before interception. Doubling/quadrupling applies while the free-fall model remains applicable. One literal defect occurs in both solutions: s/t² is said to be constant for all table pairs, although the t=0 pair gives undefined 0/0. The quotient argument requires nonzero times. The rounded readings and explicit continuation assumption support the intended ideal models; finite rounded samples do not uniquely establish exact continuous laws or measurement uncertainties. No dynamic or energy analysis of the inclined cart is needed.
reviews.passBoundaryReview: The five rows hh_motion_laws_1 through hh_motion_laws_5 each specify 3 for complete correctness, 2 for a complete response with exactly one isolated nonconceptual slip, and 0 for a missing central component or conceptual error. On the explicitly defined alphabet {0,2,3}, all 3^5=243 vectors were exhausted. Exactly 16 pass: (3,3,3,3,3), the five permutations containing one 2 and four 3s, and the ten containing two 2s and three 3s. These score 15, 14 and 13 respectively. Omitting any individual whole core gives at most 12/15. Omitting any central facet listed in the row review likewise prevents passing if the authored zero rule is enforced. Confusing uniform and accelerated motion, omitting the half-factor conceptually, or confusing average and instantaneous velocity must therefore block a pass. One or two isolated slips in different rows can pass; three such rows cannot. Error carry-forward permits wrong downstream numbers from one originating numerical slip without repeated deductions, so passing does not guarantee every numerical answer is correct. It must not erase an originating conceptual failure or excuse a new independent error. The policy is incomplete for two or more independent nonconceptual slips within one otherwise complete row and for some noncentral omissions: 3 and 2 do not apply, while the stated zero conditions need not apply. No 1-point award is authored. Thus the vector enumeration exhausts defined outcomes, but the authored response-to-score policy is not total.

reviews.directWholeGoalClaimReview: The exact claimed target is 262f807a-30d0-503e-986f-856cbd048e8e: determine both laws from graphs for uniform and uniformly accelerated motions, explain their relationship and predict position and velocity. Rows 1–4 elicit all these named operations; row 5 applies the accelerated model to supplied free fall. The spatial law can be recalled and checked in row 2, while row 3 requires an explanation of its relationship to the velocity law. This is substantive direct assessment of the target in the supplied lower-stage cases. Its evidence is bounded to positive monotone motion, chosen origins and accelerated starts from rest. The current target does not expressly contain that restriction, and the proposal description cannot redefine it. A pass therefore cannot establish arbitrary initial velocities, shifted origins or reversals. I retain the target ID as the intended coverage recommendation, conditional on correction and preparation review; this is not unconditional whole-goal certification of the frozen bytes. No additional covered goal, planning credit or proof of two independently taught cases follows.

reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: All intended ideal-model arithmetic is correct. The pendulum has 1.0 J potential energy at A; D has 0.25 J potential and 0.75 J kinetic energy; B has 1.0 J kinetic energy. Ideal C is 20.0 cm above B. The stated 19.8 cm reading differs by 0.2 cm, or 1%, and corresponds to 0.99 J mechanical energy if taken literally. This does not establish agreement within measurement uncertainty: none is supplied, and the solution invents reading accuracy. Small losses are a plausible explanation, not a demonstrated uncertainty allowance. The nail prediction of 20 cm is physically feasible under the ordinary ideal light-string/fixed-peg model: the effective length is 0.50 m, and the turning point remains below the peg with a taut string. No advanced circular-dynamics calculation is needed. At 14 cm the mechanical energy is 0.70 J, a 0.30 J reduction, although no calculation is required. Trampoline heights relative to T are 1.50, 0.50 and 0 m, giving energy triples (potential, kinetic, elastic) of (600,0,0), (200,400,0) and (0,0,600) J. Passive return to the original height and internal chemical-energy conversion during active leg extension are correct in the stated ideal model. Task 4's key is scientifically defective: a closed room is not necessarily isolated. Enlarging the system must preserve consistent inclusion of Earth and distinguish transfers across its boundary from internal dissipation. Support friction may be internal when the support belongs to the Earth assembly; excluded air provides an external transfer channel. Mechanical-energy loss need not all become only air/support thermal energy.
reviews.passBoundaryReview: The six rows sn_energy_conservation_1 through sn_energy_conservation_6 each nominally allow {0,2,3}. All 3^6=729 vectors were exhausted: exactly 22 pass at 16/18, comprising all 3s (18 points), six permutations with one 2 (17), and fifteen with two 2s (16). Omitting any individual whole core leaves at most 15/18. Any central-facet omission or conceptual failure likewise blocks passing if its row receives the mandated zero. One or two isolated-slip rows can pass; three cannot. Carry-forward permits several wrong final numbers from one originating slip, while preserving credit for independently correct later methods. It cannot erase conceptual failures or new independent errors. The policy leaves multiple independent nonconceptual slips in one otherwise complete row unassigned and supplies no 1-point tier. It also conflicts internally: a greater/smaller nail height or changing balance total is categorically listed as conceptual zero, although either can result from one division/addition slip that otherwise qualifies for 2. More seriously, row 2 requires the measurement to be judged fitting. A scientifically sound answer identifying the 1% discrepancy and insufficient uncertainty information risks zero for a central facet, hence a false fail at a maximum of 15/18. The room-isolation key creates another false-fail risk. Raising the threshold cannot repair these scientific scoring problems.
